description: Cost-minimizing multi-channel notification router for customer/staff-facing events (POS income tickets, expense alerts, generic messaging). One row per dispatch decision, not per channel: records which channel was preferred, which one actually carried the message, and the full attempt history so a fallback is auditable after the fact. Cascade order is push -> whatsapp -> sms by default (push is free, WhatsApp is cheaper than SMS, SMS is last resort). OTP and other security-critical sends bypass this cascade entirely and go straight to sms via the existing OTP flow -- notificationDispatch is not used for OTP. Fase 2 (2026-10-29): adds campaign linkage (campaignId), interaction (readAt for WhatsApp, openedAt for push taps), and cost (billable, pricingCategory, costAmount, costCurrency, costSource) so the Notification Center can compare campaigns and channels; adds an aggregate analytics endpoint so the screen stops downloading every row.

fields.name: sourceType
fields.description: Domain event that triggered this notification. Allowed values: income, expense, ticket, campaign (extensible later to loan, p2p). 'campaign' = a broadcast send from notificationCampaigns; sourceId is then the notificationCampaignId. Selects which row in notificationDispatch_policy governs the cascade for this event.

fields.name: sourceId
fields.description: Id of the originating record in its own domain table (incomeId, expenseId, ticketId), interpreted according to sourceType. Polymorphic by design -- no single fk_table applies, so no FK is declared here.

fields.name: recipientType
fields.description: Who receives the message. Allowed values: client, user (internal staff). Needed because recipientId is also polymorphic.

fields.name: recipientId
fields.description: clients.clientId or users.userId depending on recipientType. Polymorphic -- no FK enforced at the DB level, resolved in application code from recipientType.

fields.name: eventName
fields.description: Cascade policy key looked up in notificationDispatch_policy, e.g. income_created, expense_created, ticket_ready. Determines the ordered channel list and whether SMS fallback is permitted for this event -- this is what keeps the priority list data-driven instead of hardcoded in the router.

fields.name: preferredChannel
fields.description: First channel the router attempted, per the eventName policy. Allowed values: push, whatsapp, sms.

fields.name: selectedChannel
fields.description: Channel that actually carried the message. Equals preferredChannel unless a fallback occurred. Allowed values: push, whatsapp, sms.

fields.name: attemptedChannels
fields.description: JSON array logging every attempt in cascade order: each entry holds the channel name, the outcome code, and a timestamp. Source for the cost-avoidance report (percent delivered on push vs whatsapp vs sms).

fields.name: fallbackReason
fields.description: Why the router moved past preferredChannel. Allowed values: NO_DEVICE (no registered/active push target -- fall through immediately, do not attempt a send), PUSH_REJECTED (provider returned a hard rejection, e.g. invalid registration), PUSH_TIMEOUT (no response within the provider timeout), WHATSAPP_UNAVAILABLE (Twilio error, including a 63016-shaped 24h-window rejection), MANUAL_OVERRIDE. Null when preferredChannel succeeded on the first attempt. Business rule: PUSH_TIMEOUT and PUSH_REJECTED both advance the cascade to whatsapp next, same as NO_DEVICE -- none of them may skip directly to sms. Only a whatsapp-stage failure (WHATSAPP_UNAVAILABLE) may advance to sms.

fields.name: status
fields.description: pending -> sent -> confirmed, or failed. FK to notificationDispatch_status.statusCode. 'confirmed' means the provider's own delivery callback came back positive for selectedChannel (Twilio delivered/read status webhook, or a push read receipt) -- this is a channel-delivery confirmation, not a money-movement confirmation like transactionNotifications.status. A WhatsApp 'read' receipt still sets confirmed (it implies delivery) but ALSO stamps readAt -- it must no longer be collapsed into confirmed and lost.

fields.name: providerMessageId
fields.description: Twilio messageSid (whatsapp/sms) or Azure Notification Hub notification id for selectedChannel. Used to correlate an inbound provider delivery webhook back to this row.

fields.name: providerName
fields.description: Which integration actually handled selectedChannel: twilio_whatsapp, twilio_sms, or azure_notification_hub.

fields.name: messagePreview
fields.description: Short human-readable summary of what was sent (e.g. the ticket receipt link, an expense-alert title) -- deliberately not the full message body, to limit stored PII per the observability redaction rules.

fields.name: sentAt
fields.description: When selectedChannel's dispatch attempt fired.

fields.name: confirmedAt
fields.description: When the provider confirmed delivery for selectedChannel, if that channel supports a delivery callback.

fields.name: failedAt
fields.description: When status moved to failed -- i.e. every channel in the eventName's configured cascade was exhausted without success.

fields.name: providerErrorCode
fields.description: Provider error code for a FAILED send, saved for every future failure (no backfill of older rows). Twilio ErrorCode from the status callback (e.g. 63016 = WhatsApp free-form outside the 24h window, needs a template; 63003 = number not on WhatsApp; 21211 = invalid number; 30008 = unknown carrier error), or the code from a synchronous provider exception at send time. NULL while pending/sent/confirmed.

fields.name: providerErrorMessage
fields.description: Provider's human-readable error text when available (Twilio ErrorMessage / exception message), truncated to 300 chars. Never store phone numbers, message bodies or credentials here.

fields.name: campaignId
fields.description: Campaign this message belongs to (Fase 2). Set by /notificationCampaigns/send for broadcast sends, and by the dispatch cascade for transactional sends when a RUNNING always_on campaign exists for (companyId, eventName) and created_At is within its startAt/endAt. NULL for messages outside any campaign. No backfill of older rows. Index (companyId, campaignId, created_At).

fields.name: readAt
fields.description: UTC instant the provider reported the message as read (Meta WhatsApp status 'read'; Twilio WhatsApp 'read'). SMS never has it. First read wins (later duplicates do not overwrite). Measures interaction for WhatsApp; a delivered message without readAt is NOT 'not read' when the client disabled read receipts -- the UI must say 'leídos (con confirmación de lectura)'.

fields.name: openedAt
fields.description: UTC instant the client tapped the push notification. Reported by the app through POST /notificationDispatch/interaction using data.notificationDispatchId carried in the push payload (alongside data.navigationRoute). Push's only measurable interaction; Notification Hub itself has no delivery receipt.

fields.name: billable
fields.description: Whether the provider charges this message. Meta: pricing.billable from the status webhook (free-tier / service-window messages are not billable). Twilio SMS/WhatsApp: true once a price is known. Push: always false. NULL until known.

fields.name: pricingCategory
fields.description: Meta pricing category from the status webhook pricing object: marketing, utility, authentication, service. NULL for SMS/Push. Needed because Meta bills per category, and campaign sends (marketing) cost more than receipts (utility).

fields.name: costAmount
fields.description: decimal(10,4). Cost of this message in costCurrency. Twilio: the Message resource 'price' (negative in the API -- store the absolute value), fetched by a deferred job because Twilio prices settle after delivery. Meta: estimated from the company's configured rate per pricingCategory when billable = 1 (the webhook carries no amount). Push: 0. NULL while unknown -- the UI shows 'pendiente', never 0.

fields.name: costCurrency
fields.description: ISO 4217 of costAmount as reported by the provider (Twilio usually USD). The UI converts nothing: it shows the currency it got.

fields.name: costSource
fields.description: provider (amount reported by Twilio) | estimated (Meta rate card x category) | none (push). Lets the campaign card say how much of the cost is real vs estimated.

relationships.notes: Multi-tenant isolation via companyId -- injected automatically by stored procedures, same as every other module.
Informational only, not a DB-enforced FK: recipientId resolves to clients.clientId when recipientType = 'client'. See recipientType/recipientId field descriptions.
Informational only, not a DB-enforced FK: recipientId resolves to users.userId when recipientType = 'user'.
Nullable FK campaignId -> notificationCampaigns (prd_notificationCampaign.json). Deploy notificationCampaigns first.

components.name: DispatchLogFeedStep
components.description: IonList of dispatch rows, newest first: sourceType/sourceId, eventName, selectedChannel badge (push=blue, whatsapp=green, sms=orange -- orange draws the eye to the expensive channel), status badge, createdAt. IonSelect filters by sourceType/eventName/status/selectedChannel.

components.name: DispatchDetailModal
components.description: IonModal opened from a feed row: full attemptedChannels timeline (channel, outcome, timestamp per hop), fallbackReason, providerMessageId, providerName, sentAt/confirmedAt/failedAt. Answers 'why did this end up on SMS.' When status=failed, show a 'Motivo del fallo' row: providerErrorCode plus a Spanish explanation for known codes (63016/63005: WhatsApp requiere plantilla aprobada (fuera de la ventana de 24 h); 63003: el número no tiene WhatsApp; 21211: número inválido; 30008: error del operador), falling back to providerErrorMessage, or 'Sin detalle del proveedor' for rows failed before this field existed. Also show failedAt.

components.name: ChannelCostSummaryCard
components.description: Aggregate tile for a selected date range: percent of dispatches resolved on push vs whatsapp vs sms, and an estimated SMS-cost-avoided figure (count of dispatches that resolved on push or whatsapp instead of falling through to sms).

endpoints.description: Body: { companyId, sourceType, sourceId, recipientType, recipientId, eventName, messagePreview }. Idempotent per (companyId, sourceType, sourceId, eventName, recipientType, recipientId) -- recipient added in Fase 2 so a campaign broadcast (one sourceId, many clients) can send to each client once; transactional events have one recipient per source so their behavior is unchanged -- if a row already has status in (sent, confirmed) for that triple, returns it unchanged instead of re-sending. Otherwise: looks up the ordered channel list for eventName from notificationDispatch_policy, then walks it in order. For channel=push: resolve the recipient's registered push target (existing pushNotifications/registerDevice recipient-resolution logic) -- if none exists, record fallbackReason=NO_DEVICE and advance without attempting a send; otherwise call azure_notifications.send_azure_push -- a hard rejection records PUSH_REJECTED and advances, a timeout records PUSH_TIMEOUT and advances (never straight to sms -- always to the next channel in the policy list, i.e. whatsapp). For channel=whatsapp: call the existing Twilio freeform WhatsApp send (modules/ticket_notifications.py-style) -- any Twilio error, including a 63016-shaped 24h-window rejection, records fallbackReason=WHATSAPP_UNAVAILABLE and advances to sms only if sms is in the policy's channel list for this eventName. For channel=sms: call the existing Twilio SMS send -- this is always the last hop, no further fallback. Writes exactly one notificationDispatch row per call, with attemptedChannels holding every hop tried. Must wrap each provider call in timed_integration() (twilio_whatsapp / twilio_sms / azure_notification_hub) and the whole cascade in a workflow_step(), per Core Rule 6 -- the existing ticket_notifications.py and pushNotifications.py sends this module reuses do not have this instrumentation today, so it must not be silently inherited as a gap here. When a provider call raises synchronously on the LAST hop (row ends failed), store the provider error code/message in providerErrorCode/providerErrorMessage and stamp failedAt in the same write. Fase 2: accepts optional campaignId (only from /notificationCampaigns/send) and otherwise tags the row with the running always_on campaign for (companyId, eventName), if any. Push sends add data.notificationDispatchId to the payload so a tap can be reported. companyId comes from the authenticated session, not the body.

Webhook-style callback target: Twilio status callback (delivered/read/undelivered) for whatsapp/sms rows, or a push read-receipt hook for push rows. Matches by providerMessageId, updates status to confirmed (stamping confirmedAt) or failed (stamping failedAt), and appends the callback outcome to attemptedChannels for audit. On failed/undelivered it MUST also store the callback's ErrorCode in providerErrorCode and ErrorMessage (if present) in providerErrorMessage, and stamp failedAt -- the previous implementation only logged ErrorCode and left failedAt NULL, so the dispatch log could not say why a message failed. Only callbacks with a valid Twilio signature may update the row. Fase 2: a 'read' status stamps readAt (first one wins) in addition to confirmed; Meta status webhooks also write billable + pricingCategory from the pricing object and, when billable, an estimated costAmount/costCurrency with costSource='estimated'.

Body: { notificationDispatchId, type: 'opened' }. Called by the app when the user taps a push (App.tsx pushNotificationActionPerformed, reading data.notificationDispatchId). Stamps openedAt once (first tap wins); ignores ids of another company or of non-push rows. Authenticated client/user session required; never trusts a companyId from the body.

Body: { from, to, granularity: 'hour'|'day'|'week', campaignId? } (UTC). Read-only aggregate that replaces downloading every row to the browser: per bucket (Hermosillo calendar, weeks start Monday) and per channel -> total, delivered, failed, awaiting, read, opened, cost. Same delivery rules as the screen (later delivery receipt wins over an earlier failure; push is never 'delivered'). sp_notificationDispatches_analytics (@pjsonfile), companyId from the authenticated session. Also fixes the open tenant gap: _all/_one/analytics must take companyId from the session, not the request body.

Worker-only (Depends(require_worker_key)). For Twilio rows with providerMessageId and costAmount IS NULL older than 1 h, fetch the Message resource price and store costAmount/costCurrency/costSource='provider'. Batches of 100; wrapped in timed_integration('twilio_pricing'). Idempotent.
